duplicate_review.notes: Reciprocal lower-triangle league-table entries were not duplicated; each unique pairwise network comparison was extracted once using the source table upper-triangle orientation (column treatment compared with row treatment). Narrative restatements of the same numerical comparisons were not duplicated as separate quantitative atoms.

notes: Main-text prose often reports the reciprocal orientation of the supplementary league-table estimate (for example, ketamine vs etomidate RR 1.31 versus etomidate vs ketamine RR 0.77). These are mathematically reciprocal presentations of the same network comparison, not conflicts.

The title page states “Number of references: 68,” but the visible numbered reference list in the article contains entries 1-50; this production-stage inconsistency is preserved as a source limitation.

The review reports that some network estimates can differ from direct estimates because etomidate was specified as the reference in the contrast-based random-effects NMA and because of heterogeneity/unstable indirect effects.

extraction_limitations: This is a secondary systematic review/network meta-analysis rather than a primary interventional study. Quantitative atoms represent review-generated network estimates, not individual-trial treatment effects.

SUCRA values, rank probabilities, direct-vs-indirect log-risk estimates, and every conventional pairwise forest-plot estimate were not atomized as separate atoms; the clinically interpretable network effect matrix and major robustness findings were prioritized.

Outcome definitions were heterogeneous across included trials, especially hemodynamic instability and adrenal suppression; the review’s study-specific definitions were not expanded into one atom per contributing trial.
Some supplementary forest plots are image-dominant and their exact pooled numeric values are not represented in the ATOM set when the source itself did not provide a text-accessible estimate.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema is oriented to primary literature and has no first-class fields for systematic-review source type, GRADE certainty, direct/indirect/network estimate provenance, SUCRA/ranking metrics, transitivity/incoherence, or study-level contribution sets. These were preserved in tags, canonical statements, and source anchors where defensible.

The quantitative_result schema requires an exposure/comparator structure even for network-meta-analysis estimates. Each network atom therefore encodes the column treatment as intervention and row treatment as comparator, matching the league-table orientation.
